ROLE: Program entry point: validate the single <port> argument, ignore SIGPIPE, install the SIGINT/SIGTERM handler that only sets the stop flag, create the registry, the listening socket and the reactor, run the reactor, then tear down in the documented order and return the process exit status.

STRUCT.NAME: struct broker
STRUCT.ROLE: registry created first and destroyed last

STRUCT.NAME: struct loop
STRUCT.ROLE: reactor created after the registry and destroyed first

STRUCT.NAME: struct sigaction
STRUCT.ROLE: handler installation for SIGINT and SIGTERM

STRUCT.NAME: struct session
STRUCT.ROLE: not used directly; sessions are created by broker_accept through the reactor

FUNC.NAME: net_parse_port
FUNC.ROLE: turn argv[1] into a port in 1..65535

FUNC.NAME: signal
FUNC.ROLE: ignore SIGPIPE so a write to a closed peer returns EPIPE instead of killing the process

FUNC.NAME: sigaction
FUNC.ROLE: install on_signal for SIGINT and SIGTERM without SA_RESTART

FUNC.NAME: net_listen
FUNC.ROLE: create the nonblocking listening socket bound to INADDR_ANY:<port>

FUNC.NAME: loop_create
FUNC.ROLE: create the reactor bound to the registry

FUNC.NAME: loop_add_listener
FUNC.ROLE: register the listener for EPOLLIN with the NULL tag

FUNC.NAME: loop_run
FUNC.ROLE: serve clients until signalled or fatally interrupted

FUNC.NAME: loop_destroy
FUNC.ROLE: close the epoll descriptor and free the reactor

FUNC.NAME: broker_destroy
FUNC.ROLE: destroy every remaining session and free the registry

VAR.NAME: g_stop
VAR.ROLE: volatile sig_atomic_t flag written by on_signal and observed by loop_run

VAR.NAME: EXIT_SUCCESS
VAR.ROLE: status returned after a clean stop

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: net_parse_port
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 with *out_port in 1..65535 when text is a non-empty sequence of decimal digits with no sign, whitespace or trailing characters and the value fits 1..65535; -1 otherwise (empty, non-digit byte, overflow past 65535, value 0, or a NULL argument)
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: text is borrowed for the call only; nothing is allocated and nothing is retained
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1 means the argument is not a usable port: main() prints the usage line on stderr and exits 1 without creating a socket

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: net_listen
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: a non-negative listening descriptor, already O_NONBLOCK and FD_CLOEXEC with SO_REUSEADDR set and bound to INADDR_ANY:port, or -1 when socket(), setsockopt(), bind() or listen() failed (for example EADDRINUSE)
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: the returned descriptor is owned by main(), which releases it once with net_close_fd(&listener) during teardown; on -1 no descriptor is returned and the caller owns nothing
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1: main() destroys the registry it already created and exits 1 without starting the reactor; no descriptor leaks

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: broker_create
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 with *out_broker pointing to an empty registry (no sessions) or -1 on a NULL argument or allocation failure, in which case *out_broker is NULL
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: the registry is owned by main() until broker_destroy() releases it; it borrows no descriptors
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1: main() exits 1 immediately because no other resource has been acquired yet

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: loop_create
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 with *out_loop pointing to a reactor owning one epoll descriptor, or -1 when an argument is NULL or epoll_create1/allocations failed (*out_loop then NULL)
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: the reactor is owned by main() and borrows the registry and later the listener; the registry must outlive it
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1: main() closes the listener with net_close_fd, destroys the registry and exits 1

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: loop_add_listener
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 when the listener is registered for EPOLLIN with the NULL event tag, -1 for a NULL loop, a negative descriptor or an epoll_ctl failure (for example EEXIST)
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: no ownership moves: the listener stays owned by main() and is closed only by net_close_fd during teardown
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1: main() destroys the reactor, closes the listener, destroys the registry and exits 1, so a reactor without a listener never runs

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: loop_set_stop_flag
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; the reactor records only the address, so the loop can observe a signal without any handler doing work
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: the pointed-to object (g_stop, a static object of main) stays owned by main and must outlive loop_run(); the loop never writes or frees it
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; a NULL loop makes the call a no-op

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: loop_run
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 after a clean stop requested by the published flag or loop_stop(), also for a NULL loop or a reactor without an epoll descriptor (which cannot make progress); -1 only on a fatal epoll_wait error other than EINTR
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: the reactor, the registry, the listener and all sessions stay alive; ownership is unchanged by the call
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: on -1 main() still performs the full teardown (loop_destroy, net_close_fd, broker_destroy) but returns 1 because the service ended abnormally

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: loop_destroy
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; the epoll descriptor is closed (if open) and the reactor object is freed
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: consumes the reactor; the borrowed registry and the listener descriptor are untouched, so main() must still close the listener and destroy the registry
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; a NULL argument is a no-op

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: net_close_fd
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; close(*fd) when *fd >= 0, then *fd = -1, so a second call is a no-op and the descriptor number cannot be reused accidentally
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: releases the descriptor owned by main (the listener); ownership does not move into net_close_fd
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; a NULL pointer or an already released slot is a no-op

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: broker_destroy
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; every session still in the registry is destroyed (descriptor closed if still open, buffers, client identifier and filter copies freed), then the session array, the scratch buffer and the registry are freed
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: consumes the registry returned by broker_create and every session in it; afterwards no session pointer from broker_session_at() may be used
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; a NULL argument is a no-op, and sessions already reaped are not touched again

LOGIC.INPUT: argc/argv from the shell: exactly one positional argument, the decimal TCP port to listen on.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1. If argc != 2: write a usage line naming the program and the <port> argument to stderr and return 1 (no socket is created). 2. If net_parse_port(argv[1], &port) != 0: write the same usage line to stderr and return 1. 3. signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN) so that net_write_some() to a peer that has gone away yields EPIPE instead of terminating the process. 4. Install the shutdown handler: struct sigaction sa; memset zero; sa.sa_handler = on_signal; sigemptyset(&sa.sa_mask); sa.sa_flags = 0 (deliberately WITHOUT SA_RESTART, so a blocking epoll_wait/recv is interrupted with EINTR and loop_run observes the flag); sigaction(SIGINT, &sa, NULL) and sigaction(SIGTERM, &sa, NULL); a failure of sigaction is fatal (return 1) because the broker could then be killed without releasing the port. 5. g_stop = 0. 6. broker_create(&b); if it fails return 1 (nothing else is owned yet). 7. listener = net_listen(port, MAIN_BACKLOG); if listener < 0 { broker_destroy(b); return 1; }. 8. loop_create(b, &l); if it fails { net_close_fd(&listener); broker_destroy(b); return 1; }. 9. loop_add_listener(l, listener); if it fails { loop_destroy(l); net_close_fd(&listener); broker_destroy(b); return 1; }. 10. loop_set_stop_flag(l, &g_stop). 11. rc = loop_run(l): this is the whole service lifetime; sessions are accepted, decoded, routed, flushed and reaped inside it. 12. Teardown in the documented order: loop_destroy(l) (epoll descriptor closed; no further dispatch possible), net_close_fd(&listener) (port released; further connects are refused), broker_destroy(b) (every remaining session descriptor closed exactly once, buffers, identifiers and filter copies freed, registry freed). 13. Return rc == 0 ? 0 : 1.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: Exit status 0 after a clean shutdown triggered by SIGINT/SIGTERM (loop_run returned 0) with the listening port released. Exit status 1 for a usage or port error, for a failed sigaction, and for any fatal resource failure during startup or a fatal reactor error; in every failure path the resources acquired so far are released before returning.
INVARIANTS_USED: the program takes exactly one argument, the port; no other configuration exists
signal handlers only store into the sig_atomic_t flag and ordinary code performs all cleanup
teardown order is reactor, then listener, then registry so nothing can dispatch into freed state
every descriptor has exactly one owner: the listener by main, session descriptors by their session, the epoll descriptor by the loop
a client's failure never affects the process: broken peers are closed by broker_reap through the reactor
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: The process starts with no broker state and one optional command-line argument.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: The process has exited with no open listening socket, no owned memory and no live session; all cleanup was performed by ordinary code, never by a handler.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Single-threaded; only a signal handler writes the stop flag asynchronously.

runtime: wait for the port to accept
wait for exit with a 2 s timeout

injected_failures: net_listen fails with EADDRINUSE (port already bound)

runtime: client connects, subscribes to 'x/#' with an RST-generating close (SO_LINGER 0) right after subscribing
another client connects and publishes to 'x/y'
